m: Kilis Province (Turkish: Kilis ili) is a province in southern Turkey, on the border with Syria. Its area is 1,412 km2, and its population is 147,919 (2022). The province was created in 1995 from the southern part of Gaziantep Province. The city of Kilis is home to over 75% of the inhabitants of the province; the other towns and villages are very small.

Q28136223: Kilis Museum is a museum in Kilis, Turkey.
Q1528589:
Oylum is a neighbourhood of the city Kilis, Kilis District, Kilis Province, Turkey. The village had a population of 517 in 2022.
In late 19th century, German orientalist Martin Hartmann listed the village as a settlement of 15 houses inhabited by Turks.
Q97924889: Kilis Great Mosque, in the Hacı Gümüş quarter, is the oldest and largest mosque in Kilis. Despite Ottoman-era repairs it keeps its original architecture. Its first construction date is unknown; it was rebuilt in 1388 by Hacı Halil son of Abdullah and repaired in 1912 and 1924.
